style_alignment.finding: Measured stroke width as a share of figure height: the guard family draws ~3.1 per mille, and the model keeps that share for any figure. A giant drawn at guard size in its sheet and scaled up on a larger quad therefore showed lines 1.5x (minotaur) to ~3x (cyclopes) heavier than the barbarians at display size. Prompts asking for hairlines (4K 'fine' and 'ink' passes) and a lone 4K pose (2.8 per mille) did not fix it; drawing the giant beside the guard at true scale in one 4K image did (cyclops 1.7 per mille).

style_alignment.cutout: Local, not BiRefNet: FAL's balance ran out (HTTP 403 'Exhausted balance') at the cutout step. The scenes are on flat white, so the background was flood-filled from the borders (thin ground-line strokes and enclosed pure-white pockets over 300 px count as background), the guard dropped as a separate component left of the giant (one box painted out where his spear touched the general's maul), and the edge unmixed from white. Background keying only; no line work changed. Stored cutouts are cropped and halved (premultiplied Lanczos) to keep the folder small: {name}_{pose}_cutout.png.
style_alignment.packing: scripts/pack_wildlife.py: one factor per giant fits its widest and tallest pose in the 627px cell; renderer quads 1.77 (cyclops), 1.99 (general), 1.39 (minotaur) keep the previous world heights.
